K.S.MUDAGAL J, DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Challenging the award in MVC No.265/2020 dated 16.09.2022 on the file of Prl. Senior Civil Judge,
CJM and MACT, Chikkamagaluru, the insurer has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. The appellant was respondent No.3, respondent nos. 1 to 3 were the petitioners, respondent No.4 was respondent no.2 in MVC No.265 of 2020 before the Tribunal.
Name of Respondent No.1 Sanjeev Kumar Chowhan-the Driver was deleted on the ground that he died.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Claimant Nos.1 and 2 are the parents and claimant No.3 is the sister of deceased Sadananda.
On 25.12.2019 at NC: 2023:KHC:25371-DB 6.30 p.m when Sadananda was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.no.KA-18/U-1010, near Aramane Hotel, Tarikere Town, KSRTC bus KA-57/F-3607 hit the motorcycle.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, Sadananda died on the spot.
4. On the basis of the complainant filed by one Prakasha, Police registered FIR Ex.P1 in Crime No.289/19 of Tarikere Town Police Station against the driver of the bus.
On investigation, charge sheet as per Ex.P10 was filed against the driver of the bus.

5. The claimants filed MVC No.265/2020 contending that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus, they were all dependent on the income of the deceased, therefore, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation of Rs.60 lakhs to them.

6. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 contested the petition denying the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus, age, occupation, income of the deceased and their liability to pay the compensation.

The Manager vs Smt. Durgamba on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195224679/
2 7.
In the same accident, the pillion rider by name Smt.Shobha also died.
Regarding her death, her legal representatives filed MVC No.275/2020.
The Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:25371-DB consolidated both cases, recorded common evidence and disposed of both the cases by the common award.
8. The Tribunal by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

Further, in MVC No.265/2020, the Tribunal relying on Ex.P5 P.M. Report, considered the age of the deceased as 28 years, relying on Ex.P7 the pay slip,
considered his income at Rs.23,540/-, added 50% to the same by way of future prospects, deducted 1/3rd from the same towards his personal expenses, applied `17' multiplier and awarded Rs.48,02160/- towards loss of dependency.

9. The Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.49,12,160/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl.

No . Heads Amount in  Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 48,02,160/-
 2. Loss of Estate 15,000/-
 3. Loss of consortium 40,000/-
 3. Funeral Expenses 15,000/-
 4. Love and Affection 20,000/-
 5. Transportation 20,000/-
10. The Insurer has challenged the award only on correctness of the quantum of compensation granted.

Sri A.N.Krishnaswamy, learned counsel for the appellant-Insurer NC: 2023:KHC:25371-DB submits that, as the deceased was bachelor, 50% of his income should have been deducted towards his personal expenses.
He further submits that, the Tribunal was in error in including arrears of conveyance allowance and monthly bonus also in the gross salary of the deceased.
He submits that compensation awarded on the other heads is also on the higher side.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- claimants justifies the compensation awarded on the head of loss of future income/dependency and the other heads also.
So far as the income of the deceased, he submits that, the appellants had not disputed Ex.P7 salary slip, therefore, the Tribunal was justified in taking his income at Rs.23,540/-.
ANALYSIS 12.
As already pointed out, the issue between the parties is only with regard to the quantum of the compensation awarded.

So far as the determination of age of the deceased, as there was no record,
the Tribunal rightly relied upon Ex.P5- the PM Report which indicates that the deceased was aged 28 years.
Ex. P7
the salary slip shows that the basic salary of the deceased was Rs.11,397/- and HRA per month is Rs.7,597.64.

In the salary of that month, Rs.2,400/- was added by way of NC:
2023:KHC:25371-DB conveyance allowance arrears, residual choice pay and Rs.949.37 was added by way of monthly bonus.

Though these two were not regular salary, the Tribunal without noticing The Manager vs Smt. Durgamba on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195224679/
3 that fact has taken income at Rs.23,540/- on excluding conveyance arrears and bonus, total gross salary of the deceased would be Rs.11,397 + 7597.64 = 18,994.64.
In that Rs.200 has to be deducted by way of professional tax which is the statutory deduction.
Therefore, net salary comes to Rs.18,794.64 which can be rounded off to Rs.18,795/-.

Since the deceased was bachelor, as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corpn. & another1 case, 50% of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corpn. & another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Then his income comes to Rs.9,397.50 rounded off to Rs.9,398/-.
13.

As per the Judgment in National Insurance co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.2 , for the age of 28 years, if the victim was holding a permanent job, 50% has to be super- added by way of future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case there was no permanent job or deceased was self-employed, 40% has to be added.

In this case, the claimants have not examined the 2009 (6) SCC 121 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) NC:
2023:KHC:25371-DB employer of the deceased.
However, in the cross-examination of PW.1 his employment was not denied.
Therefore, it would be just and appropriate to add 40% to his income by way of future prospects.
Therefore, the total monthly contribution of the deceased to the family comes to (9398 + 3759) Rs 13,157/-.
The applicable multiplier is `17'.
Therefore, compensation payable on the head of loss of dependency would be Rs.13,157 x 12 x 17 = Rs.26,84,028/-.
14. Claimant No.3 was a married sister living separately.
Therefore she was not entitled to any compensation.

As per the judgments in Pranay Sethi's case and Magma General Insurance Company vs. Nanu Ram Alias Churu Ram & Ors.3 , claimants are entitled to filial consortium at Rs.40,000/-
each with escalation at 10% which comes to Rs.88,000/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company vs. Nanu Ram Alias Churu Ram & Ors.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the conventional heads of funeral expenses, conveyance etc., they are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- with escalation at 10%.
Similarly, on the head of loss of estate also, claimants are entitled to Rs.15,000/- with escalation at 10%.

Therefore, compensation payable under the conventional heads of funeral, transportation of dead body and towards loss of estate due to 1(2017)16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:25371-DB death of Sadananda comes to Rs.33,000/-.

Therefore, just compensation payable to the claimants is as follows:
 Sl.No. Heads Amount in  Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 26,84,028/-
 2. Loss of Estate, funeral and 33,000/-
 transportation  3. Loss of consortium 88,000/-
 TOTAL 28,05,028/-
15.
Thus compensation of Rs.49,12,160/- awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and needs modification.
The compensation awarded shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
Therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in-part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is partly allowed.

NC: 2023:KHC:25371-DB (c) Award with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
(d) Amount in deposit and TCR shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
